title: Resolve delegated-admin role shadowing & KMS alias race during private tenant migration (urgent hotfix)
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Summary: A customer performing a cross-region private tenant migration observed missing audit events and intermittent decryption failures for tenant metadata. Root cause analysis shows two correlated issues: (1) our delegated-admin role resolver prioritized service-level role bindings over tenant-scoped delegated mappings, causing role shadowing and suppression of some audit emitters during the migration window; (2) a KMS alias reconciliation race between control-plane nodes led to transient key alias mismatches which caused Decrypt failures for encrypted tenant metadata (metadata rehydrate path).

Impact: Affected customers saw incomplete audit trails for ~3-7 minute windows during tenant moves and sporadic 403/500 errors when the control plane attempted to unwrap tenant keys. This impacted Dedicated/Private customers doing live migrations and one escalated customer (AcmeFin) who requires forensic auditability.

Repro steps:
1) Initiate tenant migration across regions with duplicated delegated-admin mappings.
2) Trigger metadata rehydrate job at control-plane nodes concurrently.
3) Observe audit events missing for role-change actions and KMS Decrypt errors in control-plane logs.

Root cause (detailed):
- RBAC: Delegated-admin resolution path checks global service roles first; when a temporary migration binding exists at tenant scope, the global binding shadowed it and the audit-emitter skipped tenant-scoped audit tag injection. This was introduced during the RBAC refactor (runtime-1.18) where we optimized role lookups for cache locality but did not fully preserve tenant-scoped audit hooks.
- KMS: During key alias refresh, nodes race to create or update KMS alias metadata. Under high concurrency the alias canonicalization function returned inconsistent canonical names (case / suffix differences), which caused alias-to-key mapping misses and Decrypt to surface errors before the alias reconciliation completed.

Mitigation already applied:
- Ingested customer logs and toggled migration throttling for the impacted customer (AcmeFin) at 2026-03-11 03:20 UTC to reduce concurrency.
- Enabled temporary fallback to last-known-good key handle for decrypts while we roll the patch (risk: short-lived stale-key reads for non-sensitive metadata, approved by security).

Proposed fix (this ticket):
1) RBAC: Change delegated-admin resolver ordering to always consult tenant-scoped bindings before global bindings when a migration flag is present; re-enable tenant audit-tag emitter path for matched delegated bindings. Add unit tests and an integration test in the private control-plane e2e suite.
2) KMS: Add deterministic alias canonicalizer (lowercase + normalized suffix) and an in-memory single-flight reconciliation lock to prevent concurrent alias-upserts across nodes. Add a backfill job to reconcile alias variants to canonical aliases for the last 30 days.
3) Add an audit guard that forces a synchronous audit flush for role-change operations during migration windows.

Rollout plan:
- Stage: patch branch -> internal canary with 2 control-plane nodes in staging (run migration smoke tests) -> `priv-2026.03.2-hotfix` rollout to affected customers with staged waves and feature flags.
- Canary window: 1h with elevated logging. If errors > 0.1% revert via feature flag.

Testing:
- Unit: 12 new RBAC tests, 6 new KMS alias tests.
- Integration: Staging migration e2e with synthetic tenant moves and KMS key wrap/unwrap cycles.
- Load: Small-scale concurrency test (50 parallel rehydrate jobs) to validate single-flight lock behavior.

Rollback: Feature-flag based rollback for RBAC change and KMS change independently. We will also stop the alias backfill if we observe unexpected Decrypt errors.

Next steps / checklist:
- [x] Draft and review patch (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/control-plane/pull/5602)
- [x] Security sign-off requested (sec-review required)
- [ ] Merge and build hotfix artifact
- [ ] Deploy to staging canary and run migration smoke tests
- [ ] Coordinate customer wave and post-deploy verification with SRE & Customer Success

Notes: Attached logs and repro harness in attachments. Confluence incident writeup will be updated after the hotfix deploy with timelines and postmortem learnings.
